name: Selfhost Podcasting – Create Podcasts Easily
author: Veda

sections.description:
Selfhost Podcasting is a clean and efficient WordPress plugin that helps you create and host multiple audio or video podcasts directly from your WordPress dashboard. It provides a clean and focused admin interface where you can enter podcast and episode details. The plugin then generates a fully formatted RSS feed that meets the technical specifications of Apple Podcasts and Spotify.

Watch this introductory video to learn about the Selfhost Podcasting.

Unlike bulky podcasting plugins that try to do everything, Selfhost Podcasting focuses on what really matters: your podcast feed. Whether you’re launching a single show, publishing video episodes, or managing a podcast network, this plugin makes it easy to generate valid, standards-compliant RSS feeds for Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and other major directories.

Key Features

  • Create and manage multiple podcast shows from a single dashboard
  • Clean, distraction-free and well-organized input forms for entering podcast and episode metadata
  • Automatically generates podcast RSS feeds that comply with Apple and Spotify guidelines
  • Supports audio and video episode media, including MP3, M4A, MP4, M4V, MOV, WebM, and VideoPress-hosted videos
  • Captures episode media length, MIME type, and extension metadata for valid RSS enclosures
  • Podcast feed preview includes an inline player for audio and video episodes
  • Supports custom fields such as episode type, season, duration, and explicit flag
  • Optional private podcasting extension supports private RSS delivery and website-only listening access
  • Lightweight with no impact on your site’s frontend
  • All data stays in your WordPress site — no lock-in

Use Cases

  • Independent creators who want to self-host their podcast
  • Agencies managing podcasts for clients
  • Developers building podcasts inside WordPress
  • Privacy-conscious publishers who want to own their RSS feed

Integrations

Podcast Player

Selfhost Podcasting now comes with built-in integration for the popular Podcast Player plugin. With this feature enabled, every new podcast episode you publish will automatically include a clean, responsive audio player powered by Podcast Player — right inside your episode post content. This means your listeners can play the episode directly from the page without any extra setup on your part. To use this feature, you must have the Podcast Player plugin installed and activated on your WordPress site.

For users who prefer not to add an embedded player automatically, this feature can be easily disabled from the Selfhost Podcasting settings. This gives you full control over how your episodes are displayed while still allowing you to take advantage of the seamless integration when you want it. By combining Selfhost Podcasting’s feed creation power with Podcast Player’s playback experience, you can offer your audience a smooth, professional, and mobile-friendly way to enjoy your content.

Thrid Party Analytics Prefix

Selfhost Podcasting now supports adding prefix URLs for third-party podcast analytics services. This feature allows you to easily integrate with services like Podtrac, Blubrry, and OP3 by simply entering the prefix URL in the plugin settings. Once added, the prefix will automatically be applied to all your podcast episode media URLs, enabling these services to track and report analytics without requiring any manual edits to your feed.

Currently supported services include:

  • Podtrac – How to manually add the Podtrac prefix to your RSS feed
  • Blubrry – Statistics Documentation
  • OP3 – Setup Guide

This gives you full flexibility to choose the analytics provider you prefer, while keeping your workflow simple and efficient.

Cloudflare R2 Bucket

Selfhost Podcasting now supports seamless integration with Cloudflare R2, allowing you to automatically upload and manage your podcast media files in a Cloudflare-powered S3-compatible storage bucket. Once you enter the required Cloudflare credentials — including your Access Key, Secret Key, Bucket name, and domain — the plugin takes care of the rest.

With this integration enabled:

New podcast episodes will have their media files automatically uploaded to your Cloudflare R2 bucket.

If you delete an episode, its associated media file will be removed from the bucket, keeping your storage clean and in sync with your content.

The process is fully automated — no additional steps are required after setup.

Cloudflare R2 offers a fast, scalable, and cost-effective storage solution, making it easier than ever to host your podcast audio and video files while retaining full control over your data. This integration empowers you to focus on creating content while the plugin handles the technical details.

Privacy

Selfhost Podcasting stores podcast and episode data in your WordPress site. Optional integrations can send data to external services only when you enable and configure them.

Analytics Prefix Integrations

If you enable a third-party analytics prefix, the plugin rewrites episode media URLs in your feed so listener requests pass through the selected provider before reaching your media host. This can allow the provider to receive request and delivery data associated with podcast downloads, such as the requested URL, time of request, IP-derived or network information, user agent, referrer, range headers, and similar HTTP request metadata, subject to the provider’s own implementation and policies.

Review the privacy terms of any analytics provider you enable:

  • Podtrac Product Privacy Statement: https://analytics.podtrac.com/product-privacy-statement
  • Blubrry Privacy Policy: https://blubrry.com/about/privacy-policy/
  • OP3 Privacy Policy: https://op3.dev/privacy

You should only enable an analytics prefix if you want that provider involved in delivery measurement for your podcast.

S3-Compatible Cloud Storage

If you enable S3-compatible storage, the plugin can upload your media files from your WordPress site to the storage provider you configure. Depending on your setup, the provider may process uploaded objects, object names, file metadata, account identifiers, access credentials, request logs, and related operational or security data under its own terms.

Supported providers may include:

  • Cloudflare R2: https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/ and https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/
  • Amazon S3 / AWS: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/UsingEncryption.html and https://aws.amazon.com/privacy/app/
  • Wasabi: https://wasabi.com/legal/privacy-policy and https://docs.wasabi.com/v1/docs/data-access-restrictions-in-the-usa-for-wasabi-users

Make sure your privacy policy explains which storage provider you use for podcast media and what data is transferred there.

Private Podcasting

If the private podcasting extension is enabled in your site build, the plugin may store subscriber names, email addresses, hashed email references, access tokens, token status, expiration dates, and usage records for private feed delivery inside your WordPress database. Private podcasts can be configured to send subscribers private RSS feed links for podcast apps or website-only listening links that require a WordPress login.

Depending on your private podcast settings, guest purchases without an existing WordPress account may be skipped for automatic website-only access or may create a WordPress user account and send the listener a password setup email. The plugin may also send email notifications containing private feed links, website listening links, or token-status updates using your site’s WordPress mail configuration.

Site owners are responsible for deciding how long that data should be retained and for responding to privacy, export, and erasure requests as required in their jurisdiction.
sections.installation:
1. Download the plugin ZIP file and upload it to your WordPress site.
  2. Go to Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin and choose the ZIP file.
  3. Click Install Now, then activate the plugin.
  4. After activation, go to Selfhost Podcasting in your WordPress admin menu to start creating your podcast feed.
  5. Add podcast-level details and then add episodes.
  6. The plugin will generate a valid RSS feed URL for each podcast you create.
sections.faq:
Can I create more than one podcast feed?

Yes, you can create multiple podcasts with their own separate feeds. Each feed is independent and fully customizable.

Are the feeds compatible with Apple Podcasts and Spotify?

Yes. The plugin generates RSS feeds that meet the requirements of both Apple Podcasts and Spotify, including fields like episode type, season, and explicit content flags.

Can I publish video podcast episodes?

Yes. Episode media fields support audio and video files, including MP4, M4V, MOV, WebM, and VideoPress-hosted videos that can be resolved to direct MP4 media files for RSS enclosures.

Can I offer private podcast access without sending listeners a private RSS feed?

Yes, when the private podcasting extension is enabled, private podcasts can use website-only listening. Eligible logged-in users can access the podcast preview page on your website, while tokenized RSS feeds can remain internal.
sections.changelog:
1.4.0

  • Add: All Episodes — a new screen listing episodes across every podcast and both storage types (the plugin’s own episode type and posts from a migrated site), with search, sort, status filters, a podcast filter, and bulk actions. Server-paginated, so it stays fast with hundreds of episodes.
  • Add: Podcast episode editing now covers the whole episode in one place — attach an episode to one or more podcasts, edit its website content and excerpt independently from the feed description, set website tags and a website featured image (separate from the feed-facing episode art), and see at a glance whether it’s ready for the feed.
  • Add: Post-typed episodes (from a PowerPress or Seriously Simple Podcasting import) are now labeled inline in the Posts list — a Podcast column, an Episodes view, and an Edit podcast data row action — without filtering them out of your normal Posts workflow.
  • Fix: The “Podcast Episodes” menu item no longer opens a dead list whose Add New silently created an episode attached to no podcast and never reaching a feed. That screen is retired; every path (menu, direct links, bookmarks) now routes to All Episodes or the podcast’s own Manage Episodes, and any episode from an older version left without a podcast is flagged with a one-click fix.
  • Modify: The per-podcast Manage Episodes screen is now server-paginated instead of rendering every episode on every page load — a podcast with hundreds of episodes now loads one page at a time.
  • Modify: Editing an episode always opens the plugin’s own episode screen, for every post type. The block editor is still reachable from a row action for episodes whose post type supports it.
  • Upgrade: existing installs get a one-time, batched background pass that backfills the new canonical podcast-attachment record for episodes that only had the legacy one; nothing is deleted or changed for episodes that already have it, and private-podcast delivery is unaffected.

1.3.5

  • Fix: Cloud storage offload no longer stops after the first episode. A single upload failure used to discard every pending upload task and silently drop newly queued ones, so no later episode was ever offloaded. Uploads now pause without losing the backlog, and resuming a paused podcast continues the queued work.
  • Fix: Uploaded media is stored with a publicly readable object ACL. Objects were previously written as private while the plugin serves them from a direct, unsigned URL, so delivery verification always failed and no episode ever received a working bucket URL. The new sh_podcasting_s3_object_acl filter can override this. Episodes uploaded before this release must be re-uploaded to become readable.
  • Fix: Re-uploading the media of an episode that was already offloaded no longer deletes the object it has just uploaded.
  • Fix: Replaced media that could not be removed from the bucket is now recorded and cleaned up on the next delete, instead of being left behind as an untracked object that keeps accruing storage cost.
  • Fix: Missing or undecryptable storage credentials now pause uploads without consuming an episode’s retry attempts and without counting as a delivery failure.
  • Fix: Podcast feeds only publish a bucket URL once the object is confirmed reachable, or when no local copy of the media is left. This prevents an unreachable enclosure URL from being published while a working local file still exists.
  • Fix: Background jobs now consider podcasts in draft, pending, private, and scheduled status. Only published podcasts were scanned before, so uploads for an unpublished podcast were never resumed.
  • Fix: Upload size verification and bucket object listing now read the storage API response correctly. Both were silently returning empty results, so a truncated upload could go undetected.
  • Fix: Deleting an episode removes any upload task still queued for it.
  • Fix: The episode media details now report the real file size instead of always showing “0 MB”, for uploaded media and for external media URLs alike.
  • Fix: Episode media longer than an hour is no longer reported in minutes only. A 75 minute episode now reads 1:15:30 rather than 75:30.
  • Modify: A failed delivery check no longer aborts an otherwise successful upload. The result is recorded on the episode and exposed through the sh_podcasting_s3_delivery_verification_failed action, and the previous abort behaviour can be restored with the sh_podcasting_s3_fail_on_delivery_verification filter.
  • Modify: Turning off cloud storage while uploads are queued now discards those tasks instead of failing them.
  • Modify: The admin header no longer sticks to the top of the screen while scrolling.
  • Modify: Removed the duplicate Create New Episode and Manage Podcasts buttons from the admin header. Both actions remain available on the page itself.

1.3.4

  • Fix: Two podcasts created with the same name no longer receive the same feed slug, and therefore no longer share a podcast GUID. Duplicate slugs are now suffixed (-2, -3, …) as WordPress does for post slugs; a podcast whose name is unused keeps its slug unchanged. Duplicate podcast titles remain allowed.
  • Fix: Restore saving on the Private Podcasting settings, which had stopped submitting after an earlier admin update.
  • Add: Private Podcasting has been redesigned. A single toggle enables or disables private access, with Access Rules and commerce integrations shown inline, and subscribers moved to their own page reachable from the sidebar and from the hub.
  • Add: Connect Services now presents each integration as its own screen, with provider tiles for third-party analytics and cloud storage.
  • Modify: Manage Podcasts cards now show their actions inline (feed, preview, manage, delete, and the migration actions on imported podcasts) instead of hiding them behind an overflow menu. Every action carries a tooltip and a screen-reader label.
  • Modify: Connect Services cards now behave consistently when an integration is switched off: the settings stay visible but inactive rather than disappearing, and choosing a provider enables the integration.
  • Modify: Stack the ecommerce plugin and product fields in the private access integrations card so they are readable in a narrow column.
  • Fix: Correct the breadcrumb label on the private podcasting subscribers screen.

1.3.3

  • Fix: Prevent fatal errors when generating RSS error feeds on PHP 8+.
  • Fix: Avoid warnings when deleting multiple stored podcast metadata keys.
  • Fix: Support multi-podcast episode ownership in preview notes and deletion cleanup.
  • Fix: Sanitize S3 endpoint and domain fields with the intended URL sanitizer.
  • Security: Remove external QR code generation for private feed URLs to avoid sending tokenized URLs to a third party. The shp_private_feed_qr_url filter no longer fires.
  • Security: Redact S3 credential data from persisted background job error logs.
  • Performance: Add request-level podcast list caching.
  • Performance: Cache private episode REST exclusion IDs with invalidation on privacy, episode, metadata, status, and deletion changes.
  • Modify: Podcast Player integration now requires explicit opt-in. Public podcasts are no longer auto-registered on save, and appear in the Podcast Player dashboard only after enabling the Podcast Player option or deliberately displaying the feed with a Podcast Player feed-based block or shortcode. Podcasts synced before this update remain connected.
  • Modify: Disabling the Podcast Player option removes the managed player and its defaults and marks the podcast disconnected locally. Existing Podcast Player dashboard records are not automatically removed and must be deleted manually from Podcast Player; automatic removal is planned for a future release.

1.3.2

  • Fix: Set RSS feed content type for custom podcast feed slugs, including HEAD requests used by feed validators.
  • Fix: Keep episode media and episode image uploaders on their correct media library types when switching between modals.

1.3.1

  • Fix: Admin UI and functionality fixes.

1.3.0

  • Add: Private podcasting delivery mode setting for private RSS feed delivery or website-only listening support.
  • Fix: Podcast Player integration checkbox styling and interaction in the admin UI.
  • Fix: Migrated VideoPress media from Seriously Simple Podcasting and PowerPress is resolved to direct media metadata during migration.

Bug Fix: VideoPress video URL issue resolved.

1.2.8

  • Add: Support video podcast episodes with supported video media enclosures.
  • Add: Resolve supported VideoPress URLs to direct MP4 episode media when available.
  • Modify: Episode media fields, validation, feed generation, and storage upload handling now support audio and video media metadata.
  • Modify: Feed preview player now supports inline playback for video episodes.

  • Modify: Improved Podcast Player Integration.

  • Add: Support Migration of podcasts from Powerpress and SSP.
  • Add: Documentation Update.

  • Add: Add support for thumbnail and post_tags for podcast episode post type.
  • Add: Settings to control RSS feed display style in browser.
